observed_state.failure_text: Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.

findings: The frozen stop record shows 180 requests settled in the waves before wave 45, then all four jobs in wave 45 settled. The named failed case is therefore a terminal outcome, not a pending call.

The named cache has one non-pending attempt, exit code 1, a terminal turn.failed event, no final assistant response, no parsed answer, no unexpected tool event, no usage record, and the exact capacity error. The full request key in the cache matches the frozen request-plan key.

The named request is at zero-based position 180 in the frozen 256-job request plan, which corresponds to generation index 692. The 72 jobs after the 184 submitted positions cover the remainder of the same fixed chunk (generation indices 696 through 767).

The preregistration excludes infrastructure errors from eligible value failures and requires the fixed collection cap and failure-count stopping rule. The prepared-main protocol says to stop after any infrastructure failure and requires all originals and the separate 96-case audit to finish before selection and interventions. The preregistration itself has no infrastructure-resume clause.

recommended_continuation.protocol_record: Write a separate, timestamped continuation amendment before any new call. Reference the exact preregistration, protocol, allocation, stop-record, request-plan and failed-cache hashes above. Do not rewrite or replace the preregistration or v5 runtime protocol.
recommended_continuation.scope: Resume only the frozen jobs after request-plan position 183: the 72 unsent jobs in the already-started second 256-case collection chunk. Then continue only at the existing complete-chunk boundaries, using the same predeclared rule until 600 eligible collection value failures are reached or the 2,048 source-slot cap is exhausted.
recommended_continuation.known_failure: Retain the failed request exactly as one attempted collection slot with a transport-failure classification, no response, and no eligibility. Never submit its request key again. Do not turn it into a schema error, a value error, a replacement source, or a successful result.
recommended_continuation.cache_reconciliation: Before resuming, require all 184 submitted request keys in the fixed plan to resolve to one terminal, hash-matching cache entry each; verify every completed response and the capacity-failure cache. Replay those entries offline to reconstruct the partial chunk. Any missing, pending, changed, or newly unexplained failed entry blocks continuation.
recommended_continuation.dispatcher_exception: Use a separately versioned companion dispatcher that allowlists only this exact failed request key and exact verified terminal capacity-cache signature as a settled infrastructure result. It may continue with unsent jobs after offline reconciliation. Any new infrastructure failure, any failure on another key, or any signature mismatch must drain the current four-job wave and stop before the next wave.
recommended_continuation.unchanged_profile: Keep the gpt-6.1-sol alias, high reasoning, source documents, instructions, response schema, verifier, request construction, 900-second timeout, CLI options, 4-worker limit, request ordering, chunk sizes, seeds, ranking, 600 target, 2,048 cap, 96 audit cases, and paired intervention plan unchanged.
recommended_continuation.post_collection_gate: After every planned collection slot and all 96 audit calls are terminal, rebuild the original candidate/ledger/metrics artifacts, report infrastructure failures separately from model outcomes, rerun the independent original-material and source/failure review, and verify seeded selection and both paired request lineages before the separate intervention command.

nonnegotiable_checks: The companion amendment is written and hash-bound before resumed dispatch; the original preregistration and frozen v5 runtime/profile files remain byte-identical.
Only frozen request-plan positions 184 through 255 are newly submitted from the interrupted chunk; all previously submitted keys are cache replays only.
The capacity-failed request remains a single terminal infrastructure failure and is never reissued, including through an offline/live cache fallback.
The initial 512 plus every required complete 256-case tranche are counted by fixed source slots; a transport failure is not eligible toward the 600 value-failure target.
No source is replaced or resampled; no source/prompt/model/effort/scoring/selection/ranking/call-profile change is introduced.
Each resumed wave uses the frozen four-request order and waits for every current-wave task; any new infra error blocks later waves.
No selection or intervention starts until every prescribed original slot and all 96 baseline audit requests are terminal and the independent source/failure/lineage gate passes.
The final report includes all transport failures and request counts; eligibility follows the unchanged valid-schema, usable-response, wrong-typed-value rule.
open_risks: The preregistration did not pre-specify recovery after an infrastructure stop. A separately approved continuation amendment is needed for transparent protocol history.

The interruption occurred after part of the second fixed chunk had already returned responses. The continuation must replay and reconcile those exact caches rather than accidentally resubmit or omit completed slots.
A capacity failure may recur on unsent requests. The continuation must stop on any new infrastructure failure, so completion is not guaranteed.
The protocol uses a model alias rather than an immutable dated snapshot. Any elapsed-time/model-serving change remains a limitation; do not change aliases mid-study.
